styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Table Mountain, Cape Point and the penguins.

styles.label: Beaches
styles.blurb: Camps Bay sunsets and Atlantic swims.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Winelands, braais and the V&A food halls.

stays.why: Central base under Table Mountain. Walk to restaurants and museums; short rides to most sights.
Safe, walkable and full of shops and food. Easy start for Robben Island ferries.
Promenade walks and ocean views. Good value and quick rides to the centre and beaches.
Beach on your doorstep and famous sunsets. Quieter at night; you'll need rides to town.

food: Try a braai (South African barbecue) and a Cape Malay curry in the Bo-Kaap.
Seafood at the V&A Waterfront or Kalk Bay harbour; ask the price before you order.
Book a Winelands lunch in Stellenbosch or Franschhoek; many estates need a booking.
Cheap eats: biltong, koeksisters and food-market stalls around the City Bowl.
Tipping is normal, around 10–15% in restaurants. Check if a service charge is already added.
more_time: Swap a city day for the Cape Winelands: a full day of tastings in Stellenbosch or Franschhoek.
Take the ferry to Robben Island for the history tour; book ahead and check weather.
Drive the Cape Peninsula loop to Cape Point and Boulders Beach penguins in one long day.

recommend.why: Three nights covers Table Mountain, the beaches and a Winelands day without rushing.

month_notes: Jan: hot and dry, highs near 26°C. Best beach month; book ahead.
Feb: warm and dry, similar to Jan. Great for the coast and mountains.
Mar: still warm at 24°C, a few more rain days. Good all-round month.
Apr: cooler at 22°C and more showers. Pack a light jacket.
May: mild at 20°C with about 7 rain days. Fewer crowds.
Jun: cool and wet, highs near 17°C with 11 rain days. Plan indoor days.
Jul: coldest month, highs around 16°C. Wet and windy; bring warm layers.
Aug: still cool at 17°C with 10 rain days. Watch the weather for mountain days.
Sep: warming to 18°C, rain easing. A quiet, good-value month.
Oct: pleasant at 21°C with 6 rain days. Good for hiking and wine farms.
Nov: warm at 22°C and drier. A strong shoulder month.
Dec: hot at 24°C and busy. Book hotels and restaurants early.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean climate: warm, dry summers and cool, wet winters. Wind and cloud can change mountain plans fast.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Warm, mostly dry days around 22–26°C. Ideal for beaches, Table Mountain and the Winelands.

items.title: Wettest: June to August
items.text: Around 10–11 rain days a month and highs near 16–17°C. Keep indoor plans ready.

items.title: Windy days
items.text: The Cape is windy, especially in summer. Check the cableway status before heading up Table Mountain.

items.title: Cold Atlantic water
items.text: The sea stays cold even in summer. Bring a wetsuit or swim briefly at Camps Bay.

items.title: Cool evenings
items.text: Nights drop to 10–18°C. A light jacket helps year-round.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, sunscreen, a hat, a rain jacket for winter, and sturdy shoes for hiking.

transit.best: Uber or Bolt for most trips; drive yourself for the peninsula and Winelands.

modes.text: No metro. Don't plan around rail inside the city.
MetroRail links the centre to the Southern Suburbs and Simon's Town, but there is no Sunday service. Safe by day; avoid night travel.
Buses cover main routes and show on Google Maps. Useful but slower than ride apps.
Uber and Bolt are the easiest way around; airport to centre costs about R150. Ignore unofficial 'airport taxi' touts.
Easy driving on good roads. Keep doors locked and avoid unknown areas after dark.
Fine in the City Bowl, Waterfront and Sea Point by day. Use rides at night or for longer trips.
